messages:
Alex: :rotating_light: Monitoring alerted on unusual KMS activity for svc-deploy. Spike in GenerateDataKey calls from an external IP and a suspicious IAM change. Quick log excerpt:
```
2026-03-20T14:05:12Z audit: user=svc-deploy action=GenerateDataKey resource=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/critical/cryptoKeys/cm-01 src_ip=91.122.45.33
2026-03-20T14:06:01Z audit: user=svc-deploy action=CreateRoleBinding resource=projects/redwood iam_binding=roles/kms.admin
```
Can we stand up an incident channel and triage?

sec-bot: [ALERT] detection=kms-unusual-key-usage severity=high src_ip=91.122.45.33 org=redwood rule=UnauthorizedKMSBinding
- Matching events: 43 in last 10m
- Action recommendation: isolate service account, preserve logs

Priya: Ack. Creating #incident-kms-1776501123 and pulling on-call. Priya -> I'll try to isolate svc-deploy and block that IP at the edge.

Jorge: On it. First ask: did GenerateDataKey succeed or fail? Need full audit payloads and the IAM policy change diff. Also capture the auth token issuer (if present).

Maya: Noted. Please do NOT rotate the primary KMS key yet unless we have a plan for re-encrypting. Best to disable access or remove binding first.

Priya: Blocking IP 91.122.45.33 at WAF now.
Command: `sudo wafctl block ip 91.122.45.33 --rule incident-1776501123`
Output:
```
2026-03-20T14:08:05Z wafctl: blocked 91.122.45.33 rule=incident-1776501123
```

Priya: Isolating service account: removing active keys and temporary deny role binding. Running: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account svc-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` then `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID` where needed.

Priya: Also applied a deny policy on KMS for svc-deploy via conditional binding. Snippet:
```
binding { role: "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter" members: ["serviceAccount:svc-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"] condition { title: "temp-deny" description: "incident containment" expression: "request.time < timestamp(\"2026-03-20T16:30:00Z\") == false" } }
```

Jorge: Good. I pulled the full audit log entries from Cloud Audit Logs and uploaded a copy to the forensics bucket: `gs://sec-forensics/1776501123/`. Preserved raw payloads and network metadata.

Sam: Compliance note: please snapshot the KMS key metadata (versions, labels), export IAM policy diff, and ensure we keep S3/GCS retention for 90 days. Also loop in Legal if there's risk of exfil.

Priya: Evidence saved. Paths:
- Audit logs: `gs://sec-forensics/1776501123/audit.log`
- WAF captures: `gs://sec-forensics/1776501123/waf.pcap`
- IAM diff: `gs://sec-forensics/1776501123/iam-diff.json`

Alex: Who issued the CreateRoleBinding? Was it an automated job or via console? Check who can impersonate svc-deploy.

Jorge: Traced the binding request to a short-lived token issued by our CI runner `runner-prod-12` at 14:05:59Z. Token issuer: `ci@github-actions`. We need to rotate that runner's credentials and inspect GitHub Actions logs for suspicious workflows.

Maya: I'll take CI side. I'm pulling GH audit logs and workflow run history for `runner-prod-12`. If a secret was exfiltrated from the repo, we need to rotate all repo secrets referenced by the runner.

Priya: Containment status update (14:25Z):
- IP blocked at WAF ✅
- svc-deploy keys rotated/deleted ✅
- Temporary deny binding applied to KMS access ✅
- Audit logs preserved to GCS ✅
- New suspicious role binding disabled/removed ✅

Jorge: Next triage steps:
1) Confirm whether any ciphertext was exported (check data egress logs).
2) Identify all resources encrypted with cm-01 and determine access attempts.
3) Rotate affected service-level credentials (CI runners, deploy pipelines).
4) Run full vuln scan on runner-prod-12 host.

Sam: Notifying Security Leadership and Legal. Drafting initial incident notification for internal stakeholders. No customer-impact evidence yet but we'll prepare messaging templates.

Alex: Good. Forensics: keep an immutable copy of current KMS key state; don't destroy key versions. If we need to rekey, we'll create cm-01-v2 and stage decryption workflows.

Priya: Adding quick remediation commands executed for record:
```
# remove suspicious role binding
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood --member=serviceAccount:svc-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/kms.admin

# list svc-deploy keys
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=svc-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com

# delete identified key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete 0123456789abcdef --iam-account=svc-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

Priya: Containment checklist completed at 14:36Z. Moving to recovery/forensics.

Maya: CI runner creds rotated and invalidated old tokens. Workflow runs around 14:04-14:07 show a `deploy.yaml` triggered at 14:05:50 from IP 91.122.45.33 — looks like an injected workflow. We'll revoker secrets and run a code audit on the workflow definitions.

Jorge: I'm flagging a possible privilege escalation vector: the runner used an org-level secret with broad permissions. Action item: remove org-level secret usage and replace with short-lived granular tokens.

Priya: Handoff for next shift / incident commander (end of shift summary):
- Incident ID: KMS-1776501123
- Start: 2026-03-20T14:05:12Z (detection)
- Containment completed: 2026-03-20T14:36:00Z
- Actions taken: IP blocked, svc-deploy keys deleted, temporary deny binding on KMS, CI runner creds rotated, audit logs captured to gs://sec-forensics/1776501123/
- Open action items: verify no ciphertext exfiltration (Jorge), rekey plan for cm-01 if needed (Alex/Jorge), review GH repo/workflow permissions and rotate any exposed secrets (Maya), prepare customer/leadership comms if exfil confirmed (Sam)
- On-call contacts: Priya (primary), Jorge (sec-eng), Maya (CI), Alex (exec contact)

Priya: Passing to next incident commander @Jorge. Please update timeline and escalate to Legal if ciphertext exfiltration is confirmed.

Jorge: Ack, taking over. I'll do a full egress analysis and post updates here. Leaving notes in the incident doc: `https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SecIncidents/pages/KMS-1776501123`
